content.comment_body: Is it possible to use alternative Modbus ports like 503 or 504? In my setup, I can read all inputs and outputs, but I am unable to perform write operations using [product_name] V7.2 and its Modbus driver. I tested with another Modbus software and it worked as expected, but not with [product_name] V7.2. Additionally, I cannot set port 502 in [product_name].
The solution was actually provided in your original thread, specifically in reply number 21: [url]

Please show exactly how you are attempting to write data in [product_name]. Upload your project file or a detailed sample— a picture alone is not sufficient for troubleshooting. In your network project image, I noticed open yellow Modbus connections. Normally, you would connect two devices and specify which acts as the client or server. Double-clicking the connection line shows the variables and their directions, but your image shows no data. You may need to review the [product_name] instructions more thoroughly to understand device communication. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces challenges setting the Modbus port (usually 502) in [product_name] software to enable write operations when using [product_name] V7.2 as a Modbus client. While another Modbus software allows successful writing, [product_name] V7.2 does not, suggesting either a product limitation or a configuration issue. The assignment of client/server roles and variable direction within [product_name] is unclear, complicating troubleshooting and overall usability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes to configure or force Modbus port 502 in [product_name] and reliably perform write operations through [product_name] V7.2.
